clue.text: Pampered, I revelled in fanciful hope

indicators.note: to revel is to make merry in a disorderly way, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spoilt person admits to having basked in an unrealistic wish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revelled' is the anagram signal for PAMPERED plus I; 'in' merely joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an unrealistic wish or castle in the air, originally an opium smoker's vision.

clue.text: Poet gives cash

definitions.meaning: Ezra, the American modernist who wrote the Cantos
sterling money, the unit of British currency

explanation.surface: A versifier hands over some money.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra the modernist writer and the British unit of currency share this spelling.

clue.text: Paddy has small lump on sprain

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it in the grid

parts.note: a pat is a small lump, as of butter
to rick is to sprain or wrench, as in ricking your neck

explanation.surface: An Irishman has a little swelling on top of a twisted joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' stacks PAT above RICK in this down entry. To rick a neck or back is everyday British usage for wrenching it.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddy is the familiar Irish pet form of this saint's name.

clue.text: Thousands turn up to help farm worker

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word that turns up is read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: a myriad is ten thousand, or loosely a countless number
aid means help

explanation.surface: Huge crowds arrive to lend a hand to an agricultural labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' sends MYRIAD upwards to give DAIRYM; 'to' simply joins it to the next piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a woman employed to milk cows and make butter works on the land.

clue.text: Choose an ingredient for paella — the Spanish supply the fish

parts.note: to elect is to choose
rice is the staple of the Spanish dish paella
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: Pick something to go in the paella and the Spaniards will bring the seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: The three pieces run across the word break; 'supply' joins them to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a South American freshwater creature that stuns prey with a shock.

clue.text: Nothing eaten by mother bird

indicators.note: what is eaten by something ends up inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
the letter O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A hen bird has had no food at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an extinct flightless giant of New Zealand.

clue.text: In short, give instructions

definitions.meaning: concise, taking little time or few words
to prepare someone with the facts and orders for a task, as a solicitor does a barrister

explanation.surface: To put it concisely: tell them what to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' only introduces the two meanings, one an adjective and one a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective meaning concise and a verb meaning to prepare someone for a task.

clue.text: Fed up with food, by the sound of it

indicators.note: tells us to say the word for meals and listen for another spelling

parts.note: board is meals provided, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: Someone seems thoroughly sick of what is on their plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the sound of it' turns BOARD, meals as in board and lodging, into its soundalike; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: weary and uninterested through tedium.

clue.text: Stamp, one in pristine condition, featuring the prince

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: something featuring an item has it within, so the abbreviation sits inside

parts.note: mint describes a coin or collectable in perfect, unused condition

explanation.surface: A collector's postage item in perfect state showing a royal's head.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all philately, with 'featuring' as the container signal, but the definition is the general word for a pressed mark rather than a postage item.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a mark pressed onto a surface, or to press such a mark.

clue.text: Even though upset, William Tecumseh Walton was an example

indicators.note: in a down clue, something upset is overturned, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: if can mean even though, as in a pleasant if dull evening
the forenames of General Sherman of the American Civil War

explanation.surface: An oddly named man is held up as a model despite being distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' is the reversal signal. The name must be split: the first two words are the American Civil War general, while Walton is Izaak, author of The Compleat Angler.
explanation.definitionFit: Izaak, who wrote The Compleat Angler, was a celebrated angler.

clue.text: Disentangle components for new unit

indicators.note: the components of the two words are their letters, to be assembled differently

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sorts out a jumble of parts for a freshly built module.
explanation.walkthrough: 'components for' is the anagram signal: the letters of NEW UNIT are parts to be reassembled.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to unravel strands that are twisted together.

clue.text: A football player — very large, incidentally

parts.note: a prop is a front-row forward in rugby football
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: A remark about a footballer, who happens to be enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: The football is rugby, where a prop is a front-row forward; OS is outsize on clothing labels.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: by the way, used to introduce a related remark.

clue.text: In time, one's seen as a first-rate specimen

indicators.note: tells us that one piece is found inside the word for a period

parts.note: a day is a period of time
one is the Roman numeral I, with the possessive S kept

explanation.surface: Eventually a person comes to be regarded as a prime example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is the container signal and 'seen as' a link. The definition is old slang for something excellent, not the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Old slang sense: an excellent person or thing, a fine example of its kind.

clue.text: Try out some cricket shot

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
a drive is a forceful stroke in cricket or golf

explanation.surface: A batsman experiments with a new stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match played over several days.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to take a car or product for a trial before buying.

clue.text: Out of doors go, as progress has been OK till-now

indicators.note: out can mean astray or wrong, so the letters that follow are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Head outside, since things have gone acceptably up to this point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' is the anagram signal, not part of 'out of doors': OF DOORS GO AS is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a stock phrase reporting that things have gone satisfactorily up to this point.

clue.text: One in service with two kings

parts.note: ER is Edwardus Rex, the cipher of King Edward
K is the chess and cards abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A courtier attends a pair of monarchs.
explanation.walkthrough: The service is the Royal Air Force, not a royal household: this is old RAF slang for an aircraftman.
explanation.definitionFit: RAF slang for an aircraftman of the lowest rank, a member of the forces.

clue.text: Emmental runs all over the place in hamper

indicators.note: things all over the place are scattered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Melted Swiss cheese oozes everywhere inside a picnic basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' is the anagram signal for EMMENTAL plus R. The hamper is a verb, not a basket; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to impede or restrict, as if catching in a net.

clue.text: I'm unfit, and I work out endlessly

indicators.note: to work something out is to rearrange it until it comes right

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone out of condition exercises at the gym without ever stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work out' is the anagram signal: the letters of I'M UNFIT AND I are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin phrase meaning to infinity, forever.

clue.text: Has to raise problems with river in a book

indicators.note: tells us that the turned pieces sit inside the abbreviation

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible in crossword usage

indicators.note: in a down clue, to raise the pieces is to write them upwards

parts.note: sums are arithmetic problems
the Dee is a river in Scotland and another on the Welsh border

explanation.surface: An author is obliged to bring up difficulties involving a waterway in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raise' applies to both the problems and the river, which go upwards together as EEDSMUS before 'in' places them; 'with' only joins the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an expression of unavoidable necessity, as in the saying about the devil driving.

clue.text: Long and severe questioning necessary to become a master mason

definitions.meaning: a harsh interrogation, as police are said to give a suspect

definitions.text: necessary to become a master mason
definitions.meaning: in Freemasonry the rank of master mason is the last of three stages of initiation

explanation.surface: A stonecutter must face a harsh interrogation to qualify.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh interrogation is said to be given this; it is also the Freemasons' final rank of initiation.

clue.text: Duck — I am seen initially in the lake

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm

indicators.note: tells us the single letter goes inside the word for a stretch of water

parts.note: a mere is a lake, as in Windermere

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A waterfowl is first spotted out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes S from 'seen' and 'in' puts it inside MERE. The duck is a verb, to plunge under water.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to plunge something under water.

clue.text: Face or back down?

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for a soft surface from right to left

parts.note: nap is the soft downy surface of cloth

explanation.surface: Should you confront the threat or retreat?
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NAP, the downy surface of cloth; 'or' is a link. The definition is slang for a person's features.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang sense: a person's features, as in deadpan.

clue.text: As a developer, I will need outside support

indicators.note: the first piece needs the second around it, so it goes inside

parts.note: a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge or arch
I is the Roman numeral for one, here spelt out

explanation.surface: Someone building houses admits to requiring external backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will need outside' is the container signal, and the numeral I has to be spelt out as a word first; 'As' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: someone who opens up new land or originates a new technique.

clue.text: Member in trouble — I will provide the creature with plates

parts.note: an arm is a limb, or member, of the body

indicators.note: tells us the contraction is placed inside the word for fuss

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble
I will contracts to I'll

explanation.surface: A club member is in a fix, so I shall fetch crockery for the animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal although it comes before both its pieces; 'provide' is a link. The plates are bony armour, not dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrowing American mammal covered in bony armour.

clue.text: 18 put out

definitions.meaning: the answer at 18 down, meaning to plunge into liquid
to extinguish a fire or a light

explanation.walkthrough: The number refers to the answer at 18 down, whose meaning is the first definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to plunge into liquid and to extinguish a flame.

clue.text: Push against being placed in an old woman's home

indicators.note: tells us the single letter is put inside the word for the dwelling

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme, there was an old woman who lived in a shoe
V, for versus, means against

explanation.surface: A campaign opposes an elderly lady being moved into care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being placed in' puts V inside SHOE, where the old woman lived in the English nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to move something with a rough thrust.

clue.text: Run over

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a run scored other than off the bat, such as a bye or wide

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket it is a run not scored off the bat; as an adjective it means surplus.

clue.text: Nobleman right to enrol in resistance movement

indicators.note: one who enrols in a group joins it, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: the Maquis were the French Resistance fighters of the Second World War

explanation.surface: An aristocrat is justified in joining the underground fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enrol in' puts R inside MAQUIS, the French wartime Resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer ranking between a duke and an earl.

clue.text: Main part of house-agent's work

indicators.note: tells us the answer is a run of letters forming part of the words that follow

explanation.surface: The principal element of what a property seller does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' signals a run of letters inside 'house-agent's'. Main is the old noun for the open ocean, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic synonym: the main is the open ocean, as in the Spanish Main.

clue.text: Rolling round, turned up fast

parts.note: the letter O is round in shape

indicators.note: turned tells us the next word is written back to front

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned
Lent is the Christian period of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Something tumbling over and over came to light quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes UP into PU. Rolling is short for rolling in money, and the fast is a period of abstinence.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang sense, as in rolling in it: very wealthy.

clue.text: Falsehood for instance about true subject

parts.note: a lie is a falsehood

indicators.note: about tells us the abbreviation before it is turned round

explanation.surface: An untruth, say, concerning a genuine topic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns EG into GE. The subject is a person owing loyalty to a lord, not a topic.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyal vassal owing allegiance to a feudal lord.

clue.text: Accountant, one getting a lot of seats for shows

definitions.note: defines a plural: the halls where audiences sit

parts.note: an auditor is an accountant who examines the books
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper manages to obtain plenty of theatre tickets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' joins the charade to the definition, and the second 'a' is used as its own letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The parts of theatres where the audience sits, each holding many places.
